A1.justification: v2 explicitly presents ShowMak3r++ as an extension of v1's ShowMak3r. Both PDFs provide readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–3, plus CMU Panoptic reconstruction results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction results and adds web-video comparisons and a penetration-loss ablation, including Table IV and Figures 11 and 17.

M1.justification: v2 replaces 3DLocator with spatio-temporal positioning incorporating trajectory and penetration penalties, and introduces Pi3 camera/geometry estimation for web videos. The cited operational components also change from Depth Pro to MoGe-2, 4D-Humans to CoMotion, and SDXL inpainting to ObjectClear. Keypoint refinement already existed in v1 Appendix B and is not wholly new.

E1.justification: v2 adds uncontrolled web videos covering dance, action, outdoor scenes, and movie clips, including Ballet, Joker, Parkour, SNU dance, and further appendix examples. These introduce challenging motion and camera conditions without auxiliary background images. Sitcoms3D and CMU Panoptic were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 9 adds MegaSaM to the existing multi-person sitcom comparison, and Figure 11 evaluates the original ShowMak3r alongside MegaSaM and Shape-of-Motion on web videos. HUGS, the stage-reconstruction baselines, and ExAvatar remain, making this a limited expansion of comparator membership.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes the reported alignment schedule from 10,000 depth-fitting plus 2,000 pose-refinement iterations to 6,000 full-loss iterations followed by 2,000 with depth loss disabled. v2 also introduces cropped-actor evaluation for the penetration ablation. The TBBT 165-image/10-test-image split and CMU eight-stage-camera/one-actor-camera setup remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 4 adds with/without trajectory-loss plots and penetration-loss visual comparisons; Table IV adds a targeted penetration-loss ablation. Existing face-refinement and actor-positioning analyses remain, so the analytical expansion concentrates on the new regularizers.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate and qualitative reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial qualitative results for web-video reconstruction and additional comparator outputs. Table IV newly reports PSNR 32.99 versus 33.57, SSIM 0.970 versus 0.971, and LPIPS 0.039 versus 0.038 without versus with penetration loss. The numbers in the original three tables and the CMU mean PSNR of 25.21 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 substantially extends the mathematical positioning formulation with robust keypoint alignment, third-order trajectory differences, a visible-vertex penetration penalty, and their combined objective in Equations 11–16. Equation 3 also corrects the Huber branch condition from absolute projected depth to absolute depth residual. These are substantive definitions and a mathematical correction, although no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from TV-show reconstruction to a unified pipeline also handling uncontrolled web videos without auxiliary background images. v2 additionally emphasizes natural 3D motion and penetration-aware positioning, while retaining actor tracking, facial reconstruction, and editing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting inconsistent framewise depth to 3D jitter and explaining penetration prevention and web-baseline failures. Its conclusion replaces v1's severe-occlusion and close-up-depth caveats with an unobserved-background limitation for web videos; it does not establish that the earlier failure modes are resolved.

D1.justification: v2 supplies new loss weights and a robust-loss scale, updates the alignment schedule, identifies the nonoverlapping TBBT shots used for alignment evaluation, and adds source-video links. v1's explicit alignment learning-rate values and early-stopping disclosure disappear. Hardware, runtime estimates, and face-network architecture details remain.

R1.justification: v1 positions ShowMak3r as the first comprehensive reconstruction method for shot-changing TV videos; v2 explicitly cites it as prior work and positions ShowMak3r++ around overcoming its applicability and positioning limitations. References also expand to MegaSaM, Pi3, newer geometry and avatar methods, and the newly adopted pipeline components.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and much existing prose remain, with targeted revisions to the title, author list, terminology, abstract, introduction, and conclusion. Actor-association pseudocode and the CMU experiment move from the appendix into the main text; the appendices are reorganized and author biographies are added.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a journal-style layout, replaces the opening teaser, redraws the pipeline, and separates its actor-reconstruction diagram. It adds trajectory/penetration displays, web-video comparison panels, and Table IV; the sitcom comparison gains a MegaSaM column. Retained figures and appendix material are also substantially resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The web-video comparisons, explicit positioning objectives, targeted trajectory/penetration analyses, and corrected Huber formula strengthen validation and technical clarity. The overall gain is moderated by predominantly qualitative support for the expanded scope and removal of v1's explicit occlusion/close-up caveats without clarifying whether the revised components resolve them.
